title: Behind the Backdrop
description: For her series "Am I What You’re Looking For?," photographer Endia Beal asked young Black women entering the workforce to dress as they would for a job interview and pose in their homes against a backdrop of an office. Beal intentionally left the edges of the backdrop visible, drawing attention to the ways Black women may feel pressure to change how they present themselves to fit into professional spaces. This photograph is featured in If Emmett Till Lived, an exhibition at Chicago’s Museum of Contemporary Photography that considers what freedom looks like in American life, including in education and the workplace.
translated_description: 在她的系列作品《我是你要找的人吗？》中，摄影师恩迪亚·比尔邀请即将进入职场的年轻黑人女性穿上她们面试时会穿的服装，在家中以办公室背景布为背景摆拍。比尔有意让背景布的边缘保持可见，以此引起人们对黑人女性可能感到的压力——为融入职业空间而改变自我呈现方式——的关注。这张照片在芝加哥当代摄影博物馆的展览《如果埃米特·蒂尔还活着》中展出，该展览探讨了美国生活中自由的面貌，包括在教育和职场中的自由。
